_notes: Authored here, unlike contracts/ which are generated from Stromy. Join table: workflow -> entitled client slugs -> the client-facing wf-* skill. Default-deny: a workflow absent from this file, or present with an empty clients object, is operator-only. Every slug must match an Entra app role in terraform/entra.tf (local.workflow_app_roles) -- adding a slug here does not grant the role. scripts/check_entitlements.py fails CI when a contract has no entry here.
_v2_notes: v2 (ORG-PLAN-206 C4) turns 'clients' from a LIST of slugs into an OBJECT keyed by slug, so each grant can carry commercial facts alongside the grant itself. ORG-PLAN-300 then made the billing fact PER CREDENTIAL: 'funding' maps a credential id to 'client' (the run resolves that client's own registered key, ambient operator copies scrubbed first) or 'operator' (Stromy's key, Stromy carries the spend). The scalar 'credential_policy' is still accepted and means 'every declared credential on this policy'; declaring BOTH for one slug is refused, because two statements of one answer can disagree. A credential named in NEITHER defaults to 'operator' and is reported as defaulted rather than decided -- lending our key is the right starting state for a new workflow, but a funding answer nobody chose must stay distinguishable from one somebody did. The v1 list form still parses as every slug on the default: registry and code deploy independently, and a file a newer parser refuses would deny every client at once.

stakeholder_analysis_workflow.note: Duke Strategies pilot (ORG-PLAN-070). Stromy is the self-client full-fleet test surface -- the wf-* skills ship in stromy-plugin, so the slug must be entitled here (validate-plugin-completeness Invariant #19) and hold the client.stromy app role. stromy has been client-funded since 2026-08-23 (ORG-PLAN-206 C6) and moved to MIXED funding on 2026-09-15 (ORG-PLAN-300): the client pays for the model tokens their own run consumes, while Stromy absorbs the six flat-rate evidence-channel subscriptions that do not divide meaningfully per client. It is also the only pair spending both wallets in one run, which is what exercises the scrub carve-out in production. dukestrategies stays wholly operator-funded: flipping an external client is a commercial act taken with that client, after their key is registered -- doing it unilaterally would fail every Duke run closed at stage credentials.

weekly_intel_workflow.note: Stromy's own weekly intelligence cron. Operator-only; not a client product.
